topics.topic: How the runner inherits the channel descriptor through bubblewrap without descriptor renumbering or preservation options
questions: How can the runner inherit the channel descriptor through bubblewrap if the module may not renumber it and may use no bubblewrap option that preserves or names it?

quotes: Every descriptor the environment needs from the parent — the write end of the runner's channel, the --info-fd pipe — MUST reach bubblewrap by inheritance, passed with subprocess pass_fds, and keeps the number it has in the parent: the module never renumbers a descriptor (no os.dup2, no preexec_fn), --info-fd names the pipe's own number, and the runner learns the channel's number from runner_arguments. bubblewrap has no option naming a descriptor to keep.
judgement.why: The passage explicitly requires inheritance via subprocess pass_fds while retaining the parent descriptor number; it does not require a bubblewrap preservation or descriptor-naming option.
